title: Can AI modeling tools really work for RTS-style, top-down game development?
author: BornYak6073
selftext:
I’m a newbie solo dev working on my first project. My strengths are in scriptwriting and mechanics, but I am absolutely drowning when it comes to the 3d modeling.

I’m building a RTS (think Red Alert style) in the Japanese Sengoku period. Since it’s a top-down view, the unit models don't need to be high-res or detailed, they just need to be recognizable and consistent.

I’m considering relying on AI modeling to bridge the gap. I've seen some posts on other subs mentioning tools like **Meshy**, **Hitem3D**, and **Tripo**.

Please, no promoters or bots. I just want to know: is anyone actually using these specific tools in their game dev pipeline? Do the results hold up once you bring them into the engine, or do you end up spending a lot of time fixing topology and optimization issues?

comments.author: Itadorijin
comments.body: They should work specially for you that don't need every model to be up close

comments.author: Stunning_Manner_2231
comments.body: You can use free tier and test it yourself but as far as I see it is quite well for games that camera looking from far away. But you should consider that if you build whole tank, its top part dont rotate seperatly. So you may create these seperatly then combining them in engine so with some code you can rotate top part seperatly from base.

replies.author: Stunning_Manner_2231
replies.body:
For topology, meshy create around 1.2 million face for each part (it depends of course) and retopology with meshy tool make it around 100k. İf you disable collision and add simple box ones and dont use direct shadow logic instead there are other approaches for fake shadows (or just dont do shadow) engines can handle those too. So you should be aware of why those faces may become problem. 

For visualy with some lighting and postprocess it is very good

comments.author: GigaTerra
comments.body: They will work, especially if used with a re-topology tool like Quad Remesher, and Quad Remesher is available for most 3D software.

comments.author: 88chilly
comments.body: For a top-down RTS it can work, especially since you don’t need high detail. The silhouettes are usually good enough. Just be ready to clean up topology and optimize it’s not really plug and play yet.
